lines: In 1947, a moth made a computer fail.
I'm a moth. We need to talk about it.
This is the Harvard Mark II.
A room full of relays: little metal switches that click open and shut to do math.
On September 9th, it started giving wrong answers.
So the team searched it, relay by relay…
and found her. A moth, stuck between the contacts.
And they did the most engineer thing possible:
they taped her into the logbook, and wrote:
"First actual case of bug being found."
Here's the part nobody tells you.
They didn't invent the word. Engineers already called glitches "bugs".
Edison wrote it in 1878.
That's the joke: an actual bug.
Bright light. Let's check if it's a lamp or a fire.
No, Grace Hopper didn't pull it out.
She was on the team, and she helped make the story famous.
So the most famous bug in history wasn't the first bug.
Just the first one with wings.
That page is kept at the Smithsonian today. Moth included.
Every time you debug something… you're talking about my family.
Stay curious. Not too close to the light.
